```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(fivethirtyeight)

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings

candy <- candy |> 
  mutate(type = case_when(
    chocolate & fruity ~ "both",
    chocolate ~ "chocolate",
    fruity ~ "fruity",
    .default = "other"
  ))

count(candy, type)
```

### Row 1

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Candies"

list(
  icon = "basket",
  color = "warning",
  value = nrow(candy))

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Number of Fruity Candies"

list(
  icon = "heart-fill",
  color = "secondary",
  value = sum(candy$type == "fruity"))


```

##  

# Sugar Rush: Does More Sugar Mean More Popular?

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(fivethirtyeight)

# sugarpercent is a 0-1 percentile, so convert to 0-100 for readability
candy <- candy_rankings |>
  mutate(sugar_pct = sugarpercent * 100,
         price_pct = pricepercent * 100)

most_sugary  <- candy |> slice_max(sugar_pct, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
least_sugary <- candy |> slice_min(sugar_pct, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
sugar_cor    <- cor(candy$sugar_pct, candy$winpercent)

```

# The Big Picture

### {Height=22%}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Most sugary candy"
list(icon = "cup-straw",
     color = "danger",
     value = paste0(most_sugary$competitorname, " (", round(most_sugary$sugar_pct), "th pct)"))

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Least sugary candy"
list(icon = "heart",
     color = "success",
     value = paste0(least_sugary$competitorname, " (", round(least_sugary$sugar_pct), "th pct)"))

```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Correlation: sugar vs. win %"
list(icon = "graph-up",
     color = "primary",
     value = round(sugar_cor, 2))

```

### Row 1

### {Height=58%}

```{r}
#| title: "Sugar vs. Popularity (hover for candy names)"

candy <- candy |>
  mutate(chocolate_label = if_else(chocolate, "Chocolate", "No chocolate"))

p <- ggplot(candy, aes(x = sugar_pct, y = winpercent)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = chocolate_label,
                 text = paste0(competitorname,
                               "<br>Sugar percentile: ", round(sugar_pct),
                               "<br>Win %: ", round(winpercent, 1))),
             size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#4A148C", fill = "#CE93D8") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Chocolate" = "#6D4C41", "No chocolate" = "#F06292"),
                     name = "") +
  labs(x = "Sugar percentile (within this candy set)",
       y = "Win % in head-to-head matchups") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

### Row 2 {height=20%}

::: {.card title="My takeaway"}
Write your 2-3 sentence answer here: does more sugar mean more popular? Use the trend line and the correlation value to back it up.
:::

```{r}
#| title: "All candies, sorted by sugar"
candy |>
  select(Candy = competitorname,
         `Sugar percentile` = sugar_pct,
         `Win %` = winpercent,
         `Price percentile` = price_pct) |>
  arrange(desc(`Sugar percentile`)) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10)) |>
  formatRound(c("Sugar percentile", "Win %", "Price percentile"), digits = 1) |>
  formatStyle("Win %",
              background = styleColorBar(range(candy$winpercent), "#F8BBD0"),
              backgroundSize = "100% 80%",
              backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
              backgroundPosition = "center")

```
